hash_format: v2 block hashes are "R-" + 128 hex chars of EvoHash-11; the "R" is a label, NOT part of the hash (hex has no R). Difficulty "0000" applies to the hex part immediately after "R-". Plain hex hashes are rejected.

v2_genesis.data: R0NI testnet v2 genesis — R- block hashes — circulating supply 100000 to start

simulation: 3 nodes as separate OS processes on ONE Linux VM (127.0.0.1:8021-8023), separate data dirs, localhost HTTP P2P. NOT multiple real VMs. Docker not available.
miner: node 1 only (single miner avoids competing forks in this demo)
topology: full mesh, ports 8021/8022/8023, each peered to the other two
mac_address_note: inbound only — no transaction was ever signed from Mac's address; we do not have his private key. A transaction FROM Mac's address requires Mac to sign in his own wallet app.

disposable_wallet.status: awaiting funding from Mac (one signed transfer in-app from genesis, suggested 1,000 R0NI)

ref.note: off-chain reference only — media stays off-chain

payload_limits.integrity: SHA-256 of original bytes + decompressed size, checked by nodes on receipt and again on extraction; payload covered by the transaction signature
payload_limits.oversize_policy: rejected — use kind 'ref' (SHA-256 + URI on-chain, media off-chain)

outbound_genesis_spend: requires Mac to sign in his own wallet app (standalone wallet-app.html). The testnet NEVER holds or uses the genesis private key. A signed transaction he creates in-app can be submitted with testnet-v2/accept_signed_tx.py, which verifies the signature and lets the node re-verify it before acceptance. No such signed transaction was provided in this run.
recommended_path: Mac makes ONE signed transfer in-app from genesis to a fresh disposable test wallet (small amount). The testnet then uses THAT disposable test wallet's keypair (test-only, generated by the testnet) for further spending tests — never the genesis key.
